evals.prompt: I want to write long-form LinkedIn articles like the ones that go viral. Good strategy?
evals.expected_output: Should correct the premise with data: articles reach about 0.69x an ordinary post (median 596 people) because they require a click. Should reframe the article as the durable asset rather than the distribution: 3x profile visits per impression, permanent, Google-indexed, more likely to be cited by AI systems. Should recommend a separate feed post as the delivery vehicle and set realistic reaction expectations.
assertions: States that articles underperform posts on reach
Cites the 0.69x multiplier or the 596 median
Reframes article as asset and post as distribution
Cites the 3x profile visits per impression benefit
Sets realistic engagement expectations rather than promising virality

evals.prompt: I'll put the link in the first comment so the post doesn't get penalized.
evals.expected_output: Should correct this as outdated: the first-comment workaround is penalized on LinkedIn as of early 2026. Should note this is the exact inverse of X, where the self-reply link remains correct, and warn against carrying habits across platforms. Should suggest alternatives: no link at all, or a newsletter edition which carries no link penalty.
assertions: Identifies the first-comment trick as now penalized on LinkedIn
Contrasts explicitly with X where it still works
Warns against carrying platform habits across
Offers the newsletter as a no-penalty alternative
Does not repeat outdated advice as current
